title: A constant ASASSN-14ko X-ray clock puts the cycle-38 optical half-rise before switch-off
abstract: We test the order of the TESS cycle-38 optical rise and the predicted X-ray switch-off. A constant clock fitted to five Swift switch-offs puts the optical half-rise 2.78 days before switch-off, with a central 95 percent interval of 0.92 to 4.63 days for 0.5-day independent X-ray scatter. A model with an optical precursor gives a similar order. If optical half-rise must follow switch-off, the measured cycle-34 Einstein Probe event bounds the next four switch-off intervals: their mean is at most 107.55 days at the median bound, with a central 95 percent interval of 106.66 to 107.97 days. A free EP dip depth weakens that interval to 106.23 to 109.70 days. Thus a shorter positive optical delay alone does not preserve the constant switch-off clock. A common trigger before both signals remains allowed. The result is conditional on source marker models and timing scatter. It is not a new X-ray measurement for cycle 38 or proof of an orbital period change.
